source.title: Liberty Mutual Insurance — Product & Segment Analysis and Derived Product Model
source.prepared: Prepared 28 July 2026 | Source: Liberty Mutual public websites and public corporate disclosures only
source.note: Public-website extraction — example carrier product model. Capgemini analysis; confidence flags per row.

tldr: Liberty Mutual publicly organizes itself into three strategic business units: US Retail Markets (USRM), Global Risk Solutions (GRS) and Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI). Only USRM and GRS write insurance products.

Across the public web estate we identified ~60 distinct product offerings spanning 4 buyer segments (individual/household, small business, mid-market, large/complex & global) and 3 non-insurance adjacencies (surety/guarantee, reinsurance, and services such as TPA, premium audit and risk control).

Those ~60 offerings collapse into SEVEN product archetypes. The archetype — not the line of business — is what actually determines how Coverages, Terms, Rating, Pricing, Underwriting Rules, Forms, Filings and Lifecycle behave. Two products in the same LOB (e.g. small-business workers comp vs. national-account workers comp) sit in different archetypes and need different data models.

The eight requested dimensions are NOT uniformly populated across archetypes. Filed rate/rule/form structures govern archetypes A1-A2; negotiated and manuscript structures govern A3-A4; surety (A5) is a three-party credit product where 'Coverage' and 'Rating' do not mean what they mean elsewhere; reinsurance (A6) is portfolio-level. A one-size product model will over-fit personal lines and break on specialty and surety.

The normalization key that works across all seven archetypes is: Product -> Coverage Part -> Coverage -> Limit/Deductible Option -> Rating Variable -> Rate Table -> Form -> Filing, with archetype-specific cardinality rules. Sheet 03 defines it; sheet 04 shows how each archetype instantiates it.

dimensions.name: Coverages
dimensions.definition: What the product promises to pay for, and how that promise is decomposed
atomicElements: peril or trigger basis (named peril, open peril, occurrence, claims-made, statutory)
dimensions.naturalKey: Coverage code + coverage-part code + product version
dimensions.cardinality: Coverage part 1:M Coverage; Coverage 1:M Limit/Deductible option; Coverage M:M Form
dimensions.systemOfRecord: Product master / PAS product model; forms library
dimensions.designNote: Consumer-facing coverage names are marketing labels, not coverage codes. The same economic coverage appears under different names by product (e.g. 'Additional Living Expenses' on home vs. renters). Normalize to an internal coverage code first.

dimensions.name: Terms
dimensions.definition: The boundaries of the promise: time, money and legal structure
atomicElements: limit structure (per occurrence, per claim, aggregate, per item, per location, blanket)
valuation basis (ACV, replacement cost, agreed value, stated amount)
dimensions.naturalKey: Term option ID + product version + state
dimensions.cardinality: Policy 1:M Term; Coverage 1:1 Valuation basis; Layer 1:1 Attachment
dimensions.designNote: Terms are where archetypes diverge most sharply. A 6-month personal auto term and a single-transaction M&A policy cannot share a term model. Model term as an archetype-scoped entity, not a global one.

dimensions.name: Rating
dimensions.definition: The deterministic algorithm that turns risk characteristics into a technical premium
atomicElements: exposure base (vehicle, dwelling, payroll, sales, square footage, receipts, bond amount, headcount)
model score inputs (insurance score, telematics score, cat model output)
dimensions.naturalKey: Rating variable code + rate table ID + effective date + state + underwriting entity
dimensions.cardinality: Rate table 1:M Rate entry; Rating step ordered 1:M; Product 1:M Rating algorithm version
dimensions.systemOfRecord: Rating engine; rate table repository; actuarial pricing models
dimensions.designNote: Rating is versioned, state-scoped AND entity-scoped simultaneously. Most product-model failures are a missing dimension on the rate table key. The atomic unit is the rate entry, not the rate table.

dimensions.name: Pricing
dimensions.definition: What the customer is actually charged after commercial judgement is applied
atomicElements: discount & surcharge stack and application order
loss-sensitive structure (large deductible, retro rating, paid-loss, captive/fronting)
dimensions.naturalKey: Pricing rule ID + product version + state + channel + effective date
dimensions.cardinality: Premium 1:M Pricing adjustment (ordered); Account 1:M Loss-sensitive parameter
dimensions.systemOfRecord: Rating engine; billing; underwriting workbench; collateral system
dimensions.designNote: Separate rating from pricing rigorously. Rating is filed and deterministic; pricing carries underwriter judgement, channel economics and negotiation. Liberty Mutual's own site proves channel is a price dimension — the Online Purchase Discount is a channel discount, and 'Products, prices, and savings may vary based on state and how you purchase.'

dimensions.name: Underwriting rules
dimensions.definition: Whether we will write it, on what paper, and who may decide
atomicElements: required data & third-party data calls (MVR, loss history, credit, property prefill, inspection, financials, cat model)
dimensions.naturalKey: Rule ID + rule version + state + entity + channel
dimensions.cardinality: Rule 1:M Condition; Rule 1:1 Outcome (accept/refer/decline/price); Authority grid 1:M Role
dimensions.systemOfRecord: Underwriting rules engine; underwriting workbench; third-party data services
dimensions.designNote: Two rule populations behave completely differently: automated straight-through rules (A1-A2) and human authority grids (A3-A6). Model both, and model the referral edge between them explicitly — that edge is where cycle time is lost.

dimensions.name: Forms
dimensions.definition: The legal document set that constitutes the contract
atomicElements: form type (policy jacket, coverage form, declarations, endorsement, exclusion, schedule, notice, application, bond form, indemnity agreement, slip)
bureau vs. proprietary vs. manuscript origin
dimensions.cardinality: Form M:M Coverage; Form 1:M Filing; Policy 1:M Form instance
dimensions.systemOfRecord: Forms library / document composition system; PAS
dimensions.designNote: Form attachment logic is executable business logic, not metadata. It is also the single most reliable place to reverse-engineer a product model from the outside, because form numbers are filed and public.

dimensions.name: Filings
dimensions.definition: The regulatory permission that makes the product sellable
atomicElements: Filing type (rate, rule, form, class plan, program)
filing method (prior approval, file-and-use, use-and-file, informational, exempt)
dimensions.naturalKey: SERFF number + state + entity + filing type
dimensions.cardinality: Filing 1:M Form; Filing 1:M Rate table; Entity 1:M Filing; Product M:M Filing
dimensions.designNote: The product is not one product. Liberty Mutual writes through 37 US underwriting entities (sheet 09), each a separate legal entity with its own filings. A 'product' is really product x state x entity x version — typically thousands of instances behind one marketing name. Under-modelling this is the most expensive mistake available.

dimensions.name: Lifecycle behaviour
dimensions.definition: How the contract and the money change state over time
atomicElements: Lifecycle event (quote, submission, clearance, indication, bind/binder, issue, endorse, cancel, reinstate, renew, non-renew, lapse, expire)
claim events and their feedback into rating & renewal
dimensions.naturalKey: Event type + policy/transaction ID + effective date + sequence number
dimensions.cardinality: Policy 1:M Transaction (ordered, effective-dated); Transaction 1:M Premium change; Policy 1:M Claim
dimensions.systemOfRecord: PAS; billing; claims; audit; reinsurance administration
dimensions.designNote: Lifecycle is the dimension that most often breaks a normalized model, because effective-dating and out-of-sequence transactions make policy state bi-temporal. Model transaction sequence and effective date as first-class keys, not audit columns. Archetype-specific events (surety exoneration, retro adjustment, bordereaux) are not exceptions to handle later — they are why the model needs to be archetype-scoped.

frameworkNote: Confidence C throughout this sheet: this is a normalized reference structure applied by analogy to standard P&C product architecture. It is Capgemini's proposed model, not Liberty Mutual's disclosed model. Validate against the client's own product master before use.

archetypes.name: Personal lines filed & rated
archetypes.productsInScope: Personal auto, homeowners, renters, condo, landlord, mobile home, motorcycle, boat, RV, ATV, classic car, personal umbrella

dimensions.Coverages: Standardized coverage grid: fixed base coverages plus a catalogue of optional coverages and endorsements. Coverage attaches to a rated risk unit (vehicle or dwelling) or to the policy.
dimensions.Terms: 6 or 12 month term. Filed limit and deductible option sets. Occurrence/per-loss basis. Valuation basis is a coverage-level attribute (ACV vs. replacement cost vs. agreed value).
dimensions.Rating: Fully algorithmic multiplicative rating plan. Exposure base = vehicle or dwelling. Class plan on driver, vehicle, property and territory characteristics, plus insurance score and telematics score.
dimensions.Pricing: Filed rates plus a discount/surcharge stack, plus tier and entity placement. Channel is a price dimension. Effectively no per-risk underwriter judgement.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Automated straight-through rules with third-party data calls (MVR, loss history, credit, property prefill, inspection). Eligibility, decline and tier-placement rules are all executable.
dimensions.Forms: Bureau-derived (ISO) plus proprietary coverage forms and endorsements, state-specific editions, declarations page composed at issue.
dimensions.Filings: Heavily filed: rate, rule and form filings per state per entity. Prior-approval states constrain speed to market. Residual market and statutory coverage obligations apply.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Quote > bind > issue > mid-term endorsement > automatic renewal with re-rate > cancel/reinstate/non-renew. Renewal is the dominant transaction by volume.

archetypes.rationale: Highest transaction volume, lowest per-transaction complexity. Automation ceiling is high. The constraint is regulatory speed-to-market and state x entity combinatorics, not underwriting judgement.

archetypes.name: Small commercial package
archetypes.productsInScope: BOP, small GL, small commercial auto, small workers comp, commercial property, inland marine, farm, small cyber, small umbrella

dimensions.Coverages: Pre-configured coverage bundles by class of business, with a constrained menu of optional coverages. Package interaction rules matter (what a BOP already includes).
dimensions.Terms: 12 month term. Per-occurrence limits plus policy aggregate. Deductible options per coverage part. Exposure is estimated at inception and trued up.
dimensions.Rating: Class code driven (industry class plan mapped from business description / NAICS-style classification). Exposure bases: sales, payroll, square footage, vehicle count, receipts. Bureau loss cost x loss cost multiplier.
dimensions.Pricing: Rate x exposure per unit, plus scheduled rating credits/debits and IRPM within filed bounds. Package discounts. Some underwriter latitude, mostly bounded.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Appetite/eligibility table by class code with straight-through processing and referral rules for out-of-appetite or over-threshold submissions. Loss-history and financial checks.
dimensions.Forms: Bureau (ISO/AAIS) plus proprietary package forms. Class-specific endorsements. Larger mandatory-form footprint than personal lines.
dimensions.Filings: Filed programs, class plans and rating rules per state per entity. Workers comp adds bureau/state-fund and statutory rate structures.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Quote > bind > issue > endorse > PREMIUM AUDIT (the defining event) > renewal > cancel/non-renew. Audit converts estimated to earned exposure and generates additional/return premium.

archetypes.rationale: The archetype most often mis-modelled by treating it as 'personal lines with more fields'. The premium-audit true-up loop and the class-code appetite table are structurally new and must be first-class in the model.

archetypes.name: Large commercial & loss-sensitive
archetypes.productsInScope: National-account workers comp, commercial auto & fleet, large GL, commercial property, multinational programmes, alternative risk, infrastructure

dimensions.Coverages: Account-level, layered, manuscript-capable. Coverage negotiated per account. Multi-line and multi-jurisdiction within one programme.
dimensions.Terms: 12 month, sometimes multi-year. Deductible/SIR, aggregate stop-loss, corridor deductible, layer attachment. Terms are negotiated, not selected from a filed menu.
dimensions.Rating: Exposure rating plus experience rating (e.g. workers comp experience modification), loss-rating and burning-cost methods. Account-specific actuarial pricing model rather than a rate table lookup.
dimensions.Pricing: Negotiated. Loss-sensitive economics dominate: large deductible, retrospective rating, paid-loss, captive and fronting arrangements. Collateral and credit terms are part of the price.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Individual account underwriting against an authority grid by limit, hazard and geography. Risk-control survey commonly required. Reinsurance/treaty compliance and referral to reinsurance.
dimensions.Forms: Bureau forms plus heavy manuscript endorsement use. Programme agreements (deductible agreement, payment agreement, collateral agreement) sit alongside the policy.
dimensions.Filings: Filed programmes plus individual-risk / (a)-rate filings and consent-to-rate mechanisms. Fronting and captive structures add filing and reinsurance-credit complexity.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Submission > clearance > indication > quote > binder > issue > programme agreements & collateral > premium audit > loss-sensitive true-up and retro adjustments over MANY YEARS > renewal.

archetypes.rationale: The critical difference from A2 is that the financial relationship outlives the policy term by years. The data model must support retro adjustments and collateral reviews on expired policies. Cycle time here is dominated by human referral and negotiation, which is exactly where atomic-task instrumentation pays.

archetypes.name: Specialty, E&S and Bermuda
archetypes.productsInScope: Management liability, professional liability, commercial cyber, environmental, healthcare liability, M&A/RWI, war & terrorism, fine art & specie, financial risk, ocean marine, stop loss, SDI, equine, Liberty Remedy, Bermuda high excess

dimensions.Coverages: Proprietary wordings. Claims-made as often as occurrence. Coverage IS the product differentiator — Liberty Mutual describes Liberty Remedy as built around bespoke coverage agreements, definitions, terms and conditions.
dimensions.Terms: Limit / attachment / retention rather than limit / deductible. Extended reporting periods and retroactive dates. Layered and quota-share participations. M&A/RWI is single-transaction, multi-year, not annual.
dimensions.Rating: Judgement and actuarial underwriting rather than a filed algorithm. Increased-limit factors, exposure models, benchmarking. Rating is an underwriter tool, not a system-of-record calculation.
dimensions.Pricing: Broker-negotiated per risk, with minimum premiums. Non-admitted business has freedom of rate and form. Market cycle and capacity drive price more than a filed rate change does.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Individual risk underwriting with referral by limit, hazard class and aggregate/cat exposure. Sanctions and territory screening are material for war/terrorism, political risk and marine.
dimensions.Forms: Proprietary manuscript wordings and slips. Surplus lines disclosure and notice requirements. Version control of wordings is the core forms problem.
dimensions.Filings: Admitted specialty is filed; SURPLUS LINES IS EXEMPT from rate and form filing but carries surplus lines tax, stamping and diligent-search obligations. Bermuda-form products sit outside US filing altogether.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Submission > indication/quote > binder > issue > mid-term endorsement > run-off / tail election > renewal. Claims-made products create a reporting-period lifecycle distinct from the policy period.

archetypes.rationale: The archetype where a personal-lines-shaped product model fails hardest. There is often no rate table and no filed form to anchor to. Anchor instead on the wording version and the layer/participation structure.

archetypes.name: Surety & guarantee
archetypes.productsInScope: Contract bonds (bid, performance, payment), commercial bonds (court, licence & permit, fidelity), international & reverse-flow bonds, Surety Xpress, Surety Plus Vista, SBA Plan B

dimensions.Coverages: NOT indemnity insurance. A three-party obligation: surety guarantees the principal's performance to the obligee, and the principal indemnifies the surety. 'Coverage' maps to bond obligation type and penal sum.
dimensions.Terms: Term is the obligation period, often defined by the underlying contract or statute rather than an annual term. Single-bond limit plus an approved aggregate programme limit for the principal.
dimensions.Rating: Rate per $1,000 of contract or bond amount, varying by bond class and credit tier. Manual/filed surety rates. Not exposure-times-relativity in the P&C sense.
dimensions.Pricing: Priced off credit quality and programme capacity. Product tiering by account size is explicit (Xpress > Vista > standard). Government programmes (SBA Plan B) alter the economics.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: CREDIT underwriting, not risk underwriting: financial statements, working capital, bonding capacity, character, experience, backlog. General Indemnity Agreement and collateral. Treasury listing ($3.1B) and SFAA context define capacity.
dimensions.Forms: The bond form is typically dictated by the obligee or by statute — the carrier does not control it. Plus General Indemnity Agreement, riders, consents of surety.
dimensions.Filings: Bond rate filings. Treasury listing for federal bonds. SBA programme approval. Obligee-mandated statutory forms sit outside the carrier's filing control.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Principal prequalification & programme approval > bond request > bond issue > rider / limit increase > project completion > RELEASE / EXONERATION > (if default) claim on bond > salvage and indemnity RECOVERY from the principal.

archetypes.rationale: Do not force surety into the P&C product model. The account (principal) and the programme, not the policy, are the primary entities. Recovery from the principal after a loss is a normal expected flow, which inverts the usual claims logic. Liberty Mutual is #1 in US and global surety, so this archetype is strategically over-weighted relative to its 11% GRS premium share.

archetypes.name: Assumed reinsurance, delegated authority & TPA
archetypes.productsInScope: Treaty & facultative reinsurance, Nationale Borg (surety/credit/political risk reinsurance), Programs (MGA/delegated authority), third party administration

dimensions.Coverages: Scope is defined by the cedant's or programme's underlying portfolio, not by a coverage grid. Quota share, excess of loss, facultative. TPA carries no coverage at all — it is a fee service.
dimensions.Terms: Contract period (risks attaching vs. losses occurring), attachment and limit per occurrence and in aggregate, reinstatements, event definitions and hours clauses.
dimensions.Rating: Exposure and experience rating of the ceded portfolio, burning-cost and cat-model output. Rating happens at portfolio level, not risk level.
dimensions.Pricing: Negotiated rate-on-line, ceding commission, sliding-scale and profit commission. Price is a treaty economics negotiation.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Cedant and programme-administrator due diligence, aggregate and cat modelling, delegated-authority binding limits and periodic underwriting audits of the delegate.
dimensions.Forms: Reinsurance slips and contract wordings; binding authority / programme agreements rather than policy forms.
dimensions.Filings: Generally outside state rate and form filing. Reinsurance credit, collateral and licensing rules apply instead. For delegated programmes, the carrier's own filings still govern the underlying policies.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Submission > quote > firm order > slip/binder > contract issue > PREMIUM AND LOSS BORDEREAUX/STATEMENT CYCLE > adjustment (sliding scale, profit commission) > commutation or renewal.

archetypes.rationale: The bordereaux and statement cycle is the operational core and has no analogue in direct insurance. For delegated programmes there are two product models in play — the carrier's and the delegate's — and reconciling them is the real work.

archetypes.name: Life & non-P&C ancillary
archetypes.productsInScope: Term life, whole life, pet insurance, identity theft

dimensions.Coverages: Life: death benefit plus riders. Pet: reimbursement of eligible veterinary cost subject to waiting periods and exclusions. Identity theft: expense reimbursement plus resolution service.
dimensions.Terms: Life: level term periods or whole-of-life; face amount; cash value. Pet: annual limit, deductible, reimbursement percentage, waiting periods. Different term logic entirely from P&C.
dimensions.Rating: Life: mortality tables, age, sex, smoker status, medical underwriting class. Pet: breed, age, species, geography. Neither uses a P&C exposure base.
dimensions.Pricing: Life: guaranteed vs. current premium scales, level premium over term. Pet: annual premium with age-based re-rating at renewal.
dimensions.Underwriting rules: Life: medical and financial underwriting, accelerated/automated underwriting engines, tele-interview, MIB/Rx/lab data. Materially different data set and regulator.
dimensions.Forms: Policy contract plus riders and application; life illustration requirements.
dimensions.Filings: Different regulatory regime: life insurance departments, policy-form and illustration filing, reserve and non-forfeiture requirements. Pet and identity theft are typically inland marine or A&H filings depending on state.
dimensions.Lifecycle behaviour: Application > underwriting > issue & delivery > premium billing > LAPSE and reinstatement > policy loans/surrender (life) > claim on death. Pet: annual renewal with age re-rate; claim per treatment.

archetypes.rationale: Small premium share but disproportionate model complexity because the regulator, the underwriting data and the lifecycle all differ. The public site does not disclose which of these are third-party underwritten or administered — confirm before including them in a unified product model.

lifecycle.whyItMatters: Rate calculation with no contractual effect; A1-A2 real-time, A3-A6 an underwriter-produced indication
Clearance (who owns the account / conflicting broker submissions) exists only where brokers compete for the same risk
A1: MVR/CLUE/credit/property prefill. A3-A4: financials, surveys, cat models. A5: credit bureau & financial statements. A7: medical/Rx/MIB
The automation boundary. Instrumenting referral rate, referral reason and referral cycle time is the highest-value measurement in the whole lifecycle
A4 quotes carry subjectivities that must be cleared before binding
A binder is coverage before the policy document exists — a distinct contractual state most product models omit
A5 executes a bond against an approved programme rather than binding a policy
A5 General Indemnity Agreement and A3 collateral agreements are contract artefacts outside the policy itself
Form attachment logic executes here; this is where the Forms dimension becomes operational
Deductible agreements, payment agreements, risk-control service plans, TPA service agreements
Out-of-sequence endorsements are the classic source of premium-calculation defects; effective-dating must be bi-temporal
The defining A2/A3 event: converts estimated exposure to earned exposure and generates additional or return premium
Survey output feeds back into the Underwriting Rules and Rating dimensions — a loop, not a one-way service
Monthly or quarterly premium and loss reporting; reconciliation is the operational core of A6
Recurs on a credit cycle independent of the policy cycle
Pro-rata vs. short-rate calculation is a filed rule in A1-A2 and a negotiated term in A3-A4
A5 inverts the logic: the surety pays the obligee and then RECOVERS from the principal under the indemnity agreement
A1 renewal is automatic and re-rated; A3-A4 renewal is a fresh negotiation. Same word, different process
State notice rules constrain A1-A2 tightly; cat-driven non-renewal is a live property issue
The A3 signature: premium keeps changing for YEARS after expiry. Any model that closes a policy at expiry cannot support this
Frees the surety's aggregate capacity for the principal — a capacity event, not a premium event
Claims-made products have a reporting lifecycle that outlives the policy period
Negotiated settlement of remaining liabilities on a treaty
For A5 this is not a recovery function bolted onto claims — it is the expected economic outcome of a bond claim

taskMap.instrumentation: The single longest cycle-time step in most carriers, and the least instrumented

taskMap.applications: Rating engine, test harness, CI pipeline
taskMap.instrumentation: Actuarial-to-implementation reconciliation is a classic defect source and a prime automation candidate

taskMap.tasks: Set discount stack and order; set tier & entity placement rules; set channel price differentials
taskMap.applications: Rating engine, underwriting rules engine, pricing committee minutes
taskMap.instrumentation: Decision rights and approval routing are usually undocumented — map the actual approver, not the policy

taskMap.tasks: Author eligibility, decline and referral rules; set thresholds; configure third-party data calls

taskMap.instrumentation: Rule count and rule overlap are strong proxies for product-model debt

taskMap.tasks: Review submission; order data; assess; refer or price; document rationale
taskMap.applications: Underwriting workbench, external data portals, email, Excel
taskMap.instrumentation: Where the atomic-task lens pays most: underwriters typically touch 5-15 applications per submission. Count them

taskMap.tasks: Draft or amend wording; assign form number & edition; set state applicability; set attachment logic
taskMap.applications: Forms library, document composition system, legal review workflow
taskMap.instrumentation: Attachment logic is executable business logic living in a document system — a structural weak point

taskMap.tasks: Assemble filing package; select filing type; submit to state via SERFF; respond to objections; track disposition; notify implementation
taskMap.applications: SERFF, filing management system, email
taskMap.instrumentation: Objection-response loops are pure cycle time and are almost never measured. Multiply by state x entity

taskMap.tasks: Schedule effective dates; align rate, rule and form versions; deploy; verify in production
taskMap.artifact: Live product version in one state for one entity
taskMap.applications: PAS, rating engine, release tooling

taskMap.tasks: Enter risk data; select coverages; view price; purchase
taskMap.applications: Consumer web quote flow, agent portal, PAS
taskMap.instrumentation: Abandonment by step is the key measure; instrument the funnel, not the outcome

taskMap.tasks: Receive submission; clear account; index documents; create file; assign underwriter
taskMap.applications: Email, submission intake tool, clearance system, document management
taskMap.instrumentation: Highest-volume, lowest-value-add task cluster in commercial. Prime AI target and easiest to quantify

taskMap.tasks: Receive request; validate; effective-date; re-rate; issue endorsement documents
taskMap.applications: PAS, billing, document composition
taskMap.instrumentation: Out-of-sequence handling is the defect hotspot; log the sequence, not just the change

taskMap.applications: Reinsurance administration system, ledger, Excel, email
taskMap.instrumentation: The classic high-volume spreadsheet-and-email process; near-total automation candidate

taskMap.tasks: Re-rate; re-underwrite; check appetite; set renewal terms; issue offer or non-renew
taskMap.applications: PAS, rules engine, underwriting workbench
taskMap.instrumentation: A1 is automatic; A3-A4 is a full re-negotiation. Do not measure them with one metric

entitiesNote: WHY THIS SHEET MATTERS TO THE PRODUCT MODEL: a 'product' is not one thing. Take personal auto — one marketing name, sold through multiple entities, in up to 51 jurisdictions, each with its own filed rates, rules and forms, each versioned over time. The true grain of the product model is Product x State x Underwriting Entity x Version. With 37 entities visible here, a single marketing product can be thousands of distinct filed instances. Any product model keyed only on product name will collapse under this and produce silently wrong rates.
sourcesNote: NOT consulted (and the highest-value next sources): SERFF state filing repositories; NAIC statutory annual statements (Schedule T, line-of-business exhibits); agent and broker portal product/appetite guides; A.M. Best and S&P company reports; state DOI rate filing dockets.
